note: Reviewed openings: WMO portals that nav build always opens (tools/lib/nav/geom/index.js tileGeometry, tools/lib/nav/grid/rasterise.js carve).

A doorway narrower than about three yards can lose to the grid's 2.08 yd columns: a jamb's moulding or reveal on a column's centre line closes it, and the room behind becomes a pocket the pack leaves out.

Each entry names a WMO by FileDataID and one of its portals (MOPT index, from the root file); every placement of that WMO gets the cut: the portal's span along its wall, `depth` yards to each side of its plane, between the portal's bottom and top.
Add an entry only for a door that is open in the game and checked against the model's portals: a portal is where the client draws one group from the next, so it is an opening by construction.
nav build keeps a tile it already built: after a change here, delete the tiles the WMO stands on (tiles/<c>/<col>_<row>.*) or build with --force, then nav pack.

openings.why: Brill's town hall (groups entry01, entry02, tower, hall): the way in is the porch and corridor, then this side door into the tower room (portal 2, entry02 to tower, 3.2 x 4 yd), then the tower into the hall (portal 3). Its jambs' mouldings and reveal sit on both of the doorway's column centre lines, so the hall and tower were a sealed pocket of 208 surfaces.
